item.title: No justification for fresh borrowing amid revenue gains — Umeh
item.description: …Says past loans failed to ease hardship …2026 capital budget yet to be implemented …Rising fuel prices show loans haven’t eased hardship …No work on Eastern Rail Line despite $3bn loan approval By Juliet Umeh Senator Victor Umeh has questioned the Federal Government’s request for fresh loans, saying there is no justification for further borrowing when the government says it has surpassed its revenue targets. Umeh, who represents Anambra Central, spoke on Channels Television’s programme, where he reacted to the President’s request for approval of additional external borrowing. He said the government should account for previous loans and show their impact on Nigerians’ lives. “From what they have told us, there is no justification for the borrowing. Since you have surpassed your revenue expectations, there is no need taking the country into a circus around borrowing all the time,” he said. Umeh said previous loans had been presented as funding for infrastructure, but Nigerians were yet to see the results. “All the borrowing plans we have approved before have been hinged on the development of infrastructure. When you ask where the money is going, you are told the government needs money for emergencies,” he said. He added: “What we want to see is how these monies you have borrowed have impacted positively on the lives of the Nigerian people.” He said the country was in distress, with living costs rising while many people lacked money. “The cost of living has become unacceptable. People don’t have money. They don’t have purchasing power in the midst of soaring costs,” he said. Citing fuel prices, he said he had bought petrol at N1,410 per litre, while diesel was selling for about N1,889 per litre. “When will these things come down? When can people buy petrol or diesel without complaints?” he asked. Umeh criticised budget implementation, saying the 2026 capital budget had yet to be implemented as October drew to a close. “In the 2026 budget, there is no implementation of the capital budget yet. This is the end of October. We have barely one month until the end of the year,” he said. He cited a previously approved loan for the eastern rail line, saying no work was under way. “Part of that $21 billion was $3 billion for the reconstruction of the Eastern Rail Line. No work is going on there,” he said. He said the government should explain whether the funds had been accessed and how they had been used before seeking more loans. Asked whether opposition lawmakers could block the request, Umeh said the governing majority had the numbers to secure its approval. “We are not rubber stamps, but you don’t have the number to say no to it,” he said. item.title: Video: ‘Please, don’t forget your children and I’ – Toluwanisings’ wife breaks down at Tribute Night
item.description: Akanbi Elizabeth, the widow of late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, broke down in tears while paying tribute to her husband at a memorial event in Ibadan, Oyo State. In a video from the tribute night held at Jogor Centre on Tuesday, Elizabeth struggled to complete her speech as she became overwhelmed with emotion while remembering her late husband. “Toluwanisings, my dear husband. I will forever miss you. Please do not forget your children and I,” she said. Several gospel artistes attended the event to honour the late singer, including Adeyinka Alaseyori, Esther Igbekele, Laolu Gbenjo, Akintayo Akinwande, SB Live, Bidemi Olaoba, Mr Gbera, Peterson Okopi and Sarah Apekeola. Nollywood actress Bimbo Oshin was also among the celebrities present at the memorial. Toluwanisings died in Ibadan on October 14, 2026, after reportedly slumping. His death has since generated controversy over allegations that efforts to obtain emergency medical care for him were unsuccessful, disagreements over his burial arrangements and calls for an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death. Following his death, the singer’s personal assistant, Babadunni Gbolabo, alleged that efforts to secure emergency medical treatment took him to between seven and eight hospitals in Ibadan. The allegations sparked public concern about access to emergency medical services and the circumstances surrounding the singer’s death. The controversy surrounding his death has also extended to his burial arrangements, with disagreements emerging between his widow and members of his paternal family over where he should be laid to rest. Meanwhile, the singer’s grandmother, Sabitiyu Olayemi, alleged that he neglected her for years, adding to the family-related controversies that emerged after his death. item.title: 2027: INEC flags questionable voter registration, probes AI-generated photo claims
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC on Tuesday said it flagged a number of questionable registration records during the physical display of the preliminary register of voters, and has begun reviewing them. It added that currently investigating reports of suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs in the register published on its website. In a statement issued on Tuesday night, the Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee, Malam Mohammed Kudu Haruna, said the Commission “has noted public concerns and reports circulating on social media regarding suspected AI-generated photographs appearing in the Preliminary Register of Voters recently published on its website.” The Commission said the online register was not a new or altered document. “The register published online on 26 October 2026 is the same preliminary register physically displayed at Registration Areas (RAs) nationwide from 9th to 15th October 2026 as part of the Display, Claims and Objections exercise,” the statement said. It explained that the questionable records had already been picked up at that stage. “During the physical display, a number of questionable registration records were identified and flagged for further examination. The Commission commenced the process of reviewing these records and taking appropriate corrective action in accordance with established procedures,” it stated. INEC added that what Nigerians can see online is the version before any of those corrections. “The online publication represents the original preliminary register and does not reflect all ongoing data-cleanup activities,” the Commission said. It stressed that the document was never meant to be the final word on who is eligible to vote. “It is important to emphasize that the preliminary register is not the final certified register. The Display, Claims and Objections exercise is specifically intended to facilitate public scrutiny, identify inaccuracies and irregularities, and enable appropriate corrections before certification,” the statement said. On the suspicious photographs, the Commission said it was looking into how they got into the register in the first place. “The Commission is also examining the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses, and will take appropriate action based on verified findings,” it said. INEC also acknowledged the citizens and stakeholders who raised the alarm. “The Commission appreciates the vigilance of citizens and stakeholders who have brought these concerns to public attention. Such scrutiny contributes to the process of improving the accuracy and integrity of the register,” the statement read. It assured the public that proven irregularities would not be swept aside. “The Commission assures Nigerians that verified irregularities will be addressed through the applicable procedures,” it said. item.title: Senate committee clears Eze Anaba, 15 other NHRC board nominees
item.description: By Henry Umoru, ABUJA THE Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters has cleared the President, Nigeria Guild of Editors, NGE, and Editor, Vanguard Newspapers, Eze Anaba, and 15 other nominees for appointment to the governing board of the National Human Rights Commission, NHRC. The committee, chaired by Senator Adeniyi Adegbonmire (APC, Ondo Central) screened the nominees as part of the legislative process for reconstituting the commission’s governing board following President Bola Tinubu’s request for Senate confirmation. The Committee will, thereafter, forward its report to the Senate for consideration at plenary, where the upper chamber will take a final position on the nominations. Speaking with journalists after the screening exercise, Anaba explained that his nomination would provide an opportunity to sustain his longstanding commitment to human rights protection, which he described as an integral part of his journalism career. The NGE President, who expressed confidence that his diverse professional backgrounds would strengthen the commission’s capacity to promote and protect the rights of Nigerians, however cautioned against making definitive commitments before the completion of the process by the Senate. “We’ve just been screened. We’ve just been confirmed. So don’t let us jump the gun. That’s number one,” he said. Anaba expressed satisfaction with the committee’s decision, adding that the Senate’s final position would determine the next stage of the process. Explaining his background in human rights advocacy, the Vanguard Editor said his professional experience had consistently brought him into contact with issues relating to the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms. “I’ve done this human rights thing all my life. It has gone together with my journalism job. So it’s going to be a continuation of what I’ve been doing,” he said. Anaba also disclosed that he had been associated with the activities of the NHRC before his nomination to its governing board, just as he expressed optimism that the incoming board, with its blend of professional expertise, would improve the commission’s performance and strengthen its contribution to human rights protection in the country. Earlier in his remarks after the screening, Adegbonmire explained that the screening exercise had been completed and that the committee’s recommendations would be presented to the Senate for consideration. He said the Senate would communicate its decision to the President through the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation after deliberating on the report. Adegbonmire clarified that the NHRC’s governing board comprises 16 members, including representatives of the Federal Ministries of Justice, Interior and Foreign Affairs. He explained that the three ministries’ representatives were not subjected to individual screening because the law specifies the offices or ranks to be represented rather than the names of particular nominees. item.title: Nasarawa 2027: Ex-IGP Adamu raises alarm over PVC buying
item.description: Former Inspector-General of Police, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, has raised concerns over alleged vote-buying and the collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) from women to prevent them from voting in the 2027 Nasarawa State governorship election. Adamu spoke in Doma Local Government Area while responding to his endorsement as the preferred governorship candidate by the Alago nation. He alleged that some political actors were buying voters’ cards to suppress participation in the election, urging residents not to surrender their PVCs for money. “Those who don’t have people following them are collecting cards in the hands of women; they are buying so as to stop them from coming out to vote,” he said. He urged anyone whose PVC had been collected to retrieve it and encouraged eligible voters to turn out on election day with their cards. “Everyone should not agree to sell their card, and everyone should come out on election day with their card,” the former police chief said. The endorsement was announced at a rally organised by the Alago Support Group for Adamu, who is seeking to govern Nasarawa State in 2027. He expressed appreciation to the group for its support, saying the endorsement had strengthened his confidence in his political ambition. Adamu also thanked God for what he described as progress in his political journey, adding that the support from the Alago community was encouraging. He said his ambition was driven by the need to improve the welfare of ordinary residents, particularly vulnerable people who, according to him, had been neglected under the present situation. “Our coming out for this election is for the common people. We came out for the common man, to see that the common man does not suffer the way they are suffering now,” he said. Adamu pledged to prioritise education, healthcare and security if elected governor, promising to pursue improvements in public services and create safer communities. “We will put people’s lives first, to see that education with quality is given to our people, health with quality our people have obtained, and the issue of security, we will see that everyone will find peace, so that people can return to their homes to sleep without any fear,” he said. He also expressed gratitude to the Alago Support Group and other supporters for their commitment to his aspiration, saying he hoped to secure victory in the 2027 election. The former IGP’s allegation of PVC collection and vote-buying was not accompanied by specific details of those allegedly involved. item.title: Nigeria records 43,000 snakebites, 2,500 deaths yearly
item.description: Experts have urged residents to avoid handling snakes and seek prompt medical attention for snakebites, as Nigeria records an estimated 43,000 cases annually. The ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‌‍‍⁠‌​‌‌​cases reportedly result in between 1,099 and 2,500 deaths yearly. The experts gave the advice at a national training workshop on snakebite handling, treatment and management at the Lekki Conservation Centre, Lagos, on Tuesday. A medical expert, Abubakar Ballah, described snakebite as a neglected tropical disease, identifying the carpet viper as responsible for about 66 per cent of snakebite deaths in Nigeria. Ballah cited the World Health Organisation estimates of 5.4 million snakebites globally each year, resulting in 81,000 to 138,000 deaths and about 400,000 cases of permanent disability. He identified Gombe, Plateau, Bauchi, Benue and Taraba as major snakebite-endemic states, particularly within the Niger-Benue trough and Sudan Savanna. According to him, farmers, herders, children and hunters are among the most vulnerable, with cases often peaking during farming, rainy and harvest seasons. Ballah identified the carpet viper, puff adder and black-necked spitting cobra as Nigeria’s three medically important snakes. He said their venom could cause severe bleeding, tissue destruction, kidney injury, neurological complications and respiratory paralysis. He warned that delayed hospital presentation and harmful first aid could worsen patients’ conditions. He said such practices include applying tight tourniquets, cutting bite wounds, using animal dung and resorting to traditional remedies. Citing clinical cases, Ballah said some patients died following delayed treatment and harmful first aid, while others recovered after early hospital presentation and appropriate care. He identified the high cost of antivenom, poor healthcare access, bad roads and inadequate blood bank services as factors contributing to snakebite deaths. According to him, antivenom costs between ₦170,000 and ₦250,000 per vial. Ballah stressed that trained healthcare personnel should administer antivenom when clinically indicated and monitor patients for allergic reactions and other complications. He called for quality antivenom supplies, proper storage, improved referral systems and community education to reduce snakebite-related deaths. In a separate presentation titled “Dangerous Snakes of Lagos State, Nigeria,” wildlife conservation expert, Dr Mark Ofua, advised residents against attempting to catch, kill or handle snakes. Ofua said snake encounters could occur in mangroves, swamps, farms, gardens, building sites, drains, compounds and stores. He urged residents to exercise caution in such environments and leave snake handling to trained personnel equipped with appropriate tools. He identified the puff adder, black-necked spitting cobra, forest cobra, green mamba and Gaboon viper among species requiring particular attention in Lagos. item.title: Meet 5 Nigerians in the diaspora appointed to global positions in 2026
item.description: Nigerians in the diaspora have continued to secure leadership positions in global companies, academic institutions and healthcare organisations, strengthening the country’s representation in global decision-making. In 2026, several Nigerian professionals received appointments spanning corporate strategy, medicine, law, public health and academic leadership, placing them in positions to influence organisational growth, healthcare policy and international cooperation. Their appointments highlight the contributions of Nigerian professionals working across different countries and industries. Here are five Nigerians in the diaspora appointed to prominent positions in 2026. 1. Ugwechi Amadi — Chief Strategy Officer, McDonald’s Nigerian-born executive Ugwechi Amadi was appointed Senior Vice President and Chief Strategy Officer of McDonald’s in July 2026, joining the American multinational fast-food company after holding senior positions in sports, retail and management consulting. Her appointment was announced on July 15, 2026, following a statement by McDonald’s Chief Financial Officer, Ian Borden. Before joining McDonald’s, Amadi served as Executive Vice President and Head of Corporate Strategy and Development at LIV Golf, where she oversaw strategic planning and business development. She previously worked at Nike as Vice President of Global Operations Strategy, contributing to initiatives involving technology, supply chain management and organisational transformation. Earlier in her career, she worked at Boston Consulting Group, advising multinational companies on corporate strategy and business performance. Amadi holds a bachelor’s degree in Brain and Cognitive Sciences from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and a doctorate in Clinical Neuroscience from the University of Oxford. Her appointment places her in a senior position overseeing strategic priorities and supporting the company’s long-term growth. 2. Professor Ibrahim Abubakar — CEO-designate, Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations Nigerian-born epidemiologist Professor Ibrahim Abubakar was appointed Chief Executive Officer-designate of the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations in August 2026. The appointment was announced on August 14, with Abubakar scheduled to join the organisation in March 2027 and formally assume leadership in April 2027. He is expected to succeed Richard Hatchett, who has led CEPI since its establishment in 2017. Abubakar is currently Vice-Provost for Health and Professor of Infectious Disease Epidemiology at University College London. He previously directed UCL’s Institute for Global Health, contributing to research and policy development in infectious diseases, migration health and public health systems. His academic work includes research on tuberculosis, epidemiology and global disease prevention. item.title: Kano Assembly approves state police
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State House of Assembly has approved the proposed constitutional amendment to allow state governments to establish and operate their own police forces. The approval was confirmed by the Majority Leader of the Assembly, Lawan Hussaini Dala, shortly after plenary on Tuesday. Dala said the lawmakers had considered and approved the proposed constitutional review to provide for the establishment of state police. “We have approved the constitutional review for the establishment of state police at plenary today,” he said. The approval followed deliberations on the proposed amendments to the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which seek to give state governments the legal authority to establish and operate their own police forces. During plenary, the lawmakers considered the constitutional alteration bill in the Committee of the Whole, deliberating on clauses one to 26 of the proposed amendment. The lawmakers had earlier adopted a motion to consider the constitutional amendment bill in the Committee of the Whole before proceeding with deliberations on its provisions. item.title: Tinubu needs another term to consolidate reforms — Tompolo
item.description: …Presents 30 vehicles for mobilisation By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Ahead of the 2027 presidential election, High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has mobilised support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in Imo State, declaring that the President means well for Nigeria and deserves another four years to consolidate his administration’s reforms. Tompolo made the declaration on Tuesday at the inauguration of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State, where he donated 30 vehicles to facilitate grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election. Represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Limited, Chief Kestin Pondi, Tompolo said the vehicles and other resources were provided to support Governor Hope Uzodimma and the movement’s campaign activities across the state. He described Tinubu as a courageous leader who prioritised Nigeria’s interests by embarking on economic reforms from the beginning of his administration in May 2023. “Our President, President Bola Tinubu, is a very courageous man. A man who puts Nigeria first. A man who loves Nigeria more than he loves himself. “A man who loves Nigeria more than the office that he is vying for. When he came into office, he did not do the normal calculations that politicians usually do. He came in and said that he wants to reform Nigeria,” Tompolo said. Relaying Tompolo’s message, Pondi said the donation was aimed at strengthening the movement’s capacity to mobilise voters for the President across the state. “Your Excellency, we have come with vehicles. We have come with resources. These vehicles you have seen, there are 30 of them. We brought them to Imo State to support you in your cause to re-elect President Bola Tinubu,” he said. Tompolo said the movement would work with Uzodimma and other political leaders to take the President’s campaign to households and communities across Imo State, adding that the newly inaugurated chapter would be available to support campaign activities whenever required. “Your Excellency, the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State is at your beck and call. Anytime you need them, call them. Give them instructions. Tell them how you want them to campaign,” he said. Speaking at the event, Governor Uzodimma commended Tompolo for providing resources to support the campaign, describing the movement as an important partner in efforts to secure another term for Tinubu. Uzodimma said his assessment of the President’s performance had convinced him that Tinubu should be given another term to complete his programmes and initiatives. “When we preach the Gospel about the All Progressives Congress government of President Bola Tinubu, we started, we were not many. But as the days go by, the efforts and activities of the government begin to trickle in. Nigerians begin to see the man called Bola Tinubu in his true colour,” he said. item.title: US Visa Bond: Full list of countries, including Nigeria, required to pay up to $20,000
item.description: The United States has listed 50 countries whose citizens must pay a visa bond of up to $20,000 when applying for certain visitor visas, including Nigeria, according to the US Department of State. The measure applies to eligible applicants for B-1 business and B-2 tourist visas travelling on passports issued by the listed countries. The bond amounts are $10,000, $15,000 or $20,000, with the specific amount determined by a consular officer during the visa interview. In a notice published on October 2, 2026, the Department of State outlined the countries subject to the visa bond programme and their respective implementation dates. The programme operates under Section 221(g)(3) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, with the department stating that the requirement applies regardless of where an applicant submits their visa application. item.title: Senate Passes bill to jail oil polluters, impose heavier fine
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- THE Senate has passed a bill that would strengthen the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) with powers to impose heavier fines and criminal penalties for oil spill violations. The bill is titled National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (Establishment) Act (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was passed after the Senate adopted the report of its Committee on Environment. The bill seeks to amend the NOSDRA Establishment Act 2006 to provide statutory backing for adequate fines and criminal sanctions to enforce environmental laws in the petroleum sector. In his presentation of the report, Chairman Senator Olubiyi Fadeyi, Senate Chief Whip Senator Tahir Monguno (Borno North) said the amendment addresses persistent pollution in the Niger Delta. He said oil spills have continued to devastate the environment and destroy livelihoods, particularly fishing and farming, in oil-producing communities. According to Monguno, existing penalties have failed to deter offenders, necessitating tougher sanctions. “The fines are not deterrent enough to deter offenders,” he told the Senate, adding that the bill introduces criminal liability for spills that damage the environment and deprive residents of their means of livelihood. The Senate dissolved into Committee of the Whole to consider the bill clause by clause and approved Clauses 1 to 12, including the short title, explanatory memorandum and long title. Upon reverting to plenary, the Senate read the bill a third time and passed it. The law is expected to boost NOSDRA’s enforcement capacity and provide a stronger framework for tackling oil spill violations. The President Godswill Akpabio hailed the Environment Committee for its work and congratulated NOSDRA on the additional powers granted by the legislation. item.title: Jigawa Assembly approves constitutional amendment for state police
item.description: ‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State House of Assembly has approved the proposed constitutional amendment seeking the establishment of state police in Nigeria. The Speaker of the House, Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin, announced the approval during plenary, saying the move was aimed at strengthening community policing and improving security across the country. He explained that the proposed amendment was transmitted to the state Assembly for consideration after its passage by the Senate and the House of Representatives. ‎According to him, the establishment of state police would help address security challenges at the grassroots by giving state governments greater responsibility for protecting lives and property. The approval is part of ongoing efforts to decentralise Nigeria’s policing system and strengthen the capacity of states to respond to security threats within their jurisdictions. The development comes after the National Assembly gave state Houses of Assembly a 30-day deadline to communicate their positions on the proposed constitutional amendment. State legislatures were directed to indicate whether they supported or opposed the bill as part of the constitutional amendment process. item.title: ‘Toluwanisings should be buried in his home, not cemetery’ – Grandma
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The paternal grandmother of late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has alleged that he rarely supported her financially before his death while opposing plans to bury him in a cemetery. The elderly woman, identified as Sabitiyu Olayemi, made the claims in a trending social media interview with journalist Dunmininu in Osun. The interview was conducted in Yoruba. She said Toluwanisings was born in Kano and also narrated how she helped care for the singer and his mother before he moved to Lagos, but had not seen him for more than five years. “Sodiq was born in Kano, that was where his naming cermony was conducted. We have been taking care of Sodiq (Toluwanisings) and his mother even before he went to Lagos. He attended Arabic schools. When he was in grammar school, I would visit him” she said, in Yoruba language. The grandmother also revealed that she knew he was a musician but did not know he had built a house or held a housewarming ceremony. She recalled that he once visited her with his wife and first child, but alleged that they had been out of touch for years. “I just knew he is a musician. I am not aware he built a house; I was not aware of a housewarming. Even if I want to call him, they will say I shouldn’t. It’s been a long time I saw him. It has been over five years I set my eyes on him,” the grandmother said. She said she eventually asked someone in the village to help her call him. “So I called and told him it was me. He responded, ‘Ahh, Mummy.’ I told him that you cannot even check up on me. He said it is work that has been a hindrance,” she recounted. According to her, Toluwanisings sent her ₦10,000 on about three occasions after that conversation, but did not send money again. She also alleged that when her phone was damaged and she sought help contacting him about a replacement, his elder sibling told her not to call him. Asked whether he sent her medication or money for medical expenses, she replied: “There is nothing Sodiq (Toluwanisings) sends to me.” Despite her allegations, she said his death deeply affected her as she broke down in tears during the interview. “When I heard that he had died, I felt so sad. Whether I benefited from him or not, he is still my child. I have accepted my fate. I wish God had taken me so I would not have had to witness this tragedy,” she said, breaking down in tears. The grandmother also objected to burying the singer in a cemetery, saying he should be laid to rest at his home. “I do not agree that Toluwanisings should be buried in a cemetery. They should bury him at his house. They should not come and bury him close to his mother,” she said. Toluwanisings’ family announced that the singer died in the early hours of October 14, 2026 at the age of 41, but did not disclose the cause of death. item.title: 2027: APM in coalition talks, says Daura
item.description: By Juliet Umeh Vice-presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Lawal Daura, says the party is involved in coalition discussions ahead of the 2027 general elections. Daura disclosed this on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily, where he also called for an inclusive approach to governance, saying Nigeria needed a “reset” to address what he described as recurring political and social problems. “We are involved right now in the discussion for the coalition,” he said. Explaining the APM’s “reset agenda,” Daura said Nigeria had been “moving in cycles without really making much or any progress.” He said the agenda would bring Nigerians together to discuss the country’s direction and agree on how it should be governed. “The reset agenda should be an all-inclusive thing. Let us get together as Nigerians.” According to him, a government formed under the agenda would involve stakeholders beyond those who helped it win an election. “Where you make an election or win your election to be the winner-takes-all is not going to help Nigeria,” he said. Daura, a former Director-General of the Department of State Services, said his decision to enter politics was motivated by his desire to contribute to the country’s development. “I felt maybe there is a need for me to come out and contribute,” he said, adding that joining the political process would allow him to contribute “more and better than when it is just maybe by the sidelines.” He said his years in public service had given him insights into the country’s challenges, but added: “I play politics, but within the definition given by politicians in Nigeria, I would say I am not a politician.” Daura said he initially sought the governorship of Katsina State after senior citizens approached him over insecurity in the state, which he described as an “epicentre” of banditry and kidnapping. “I have made myself very clear right from the onset that whatever my people requested me to do, I would do. At my level, I can even become a local government chairman. I wouldn’t mind.” He said his governorship bid through the African Democratic Congress did not proceed as he had hoped, citing the absence of primaries and concerns about compliance with electoral law. He said he declined suggestions that he seek a Senate seat instead. Daura said he chose the APM after considering other parties, which he alleged faced internal leadership disputes or court cases. He called the APM “the only healthy party” at the time he joined and said it was expanding its reach. “Right now, as I speak, APM is a party to beat,” he said. item.title: Fubara Reaffirms Support For Tinubu, Wike-Led Rainbow Coalition
item.description: Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has reaffirmed his support for President Bola Tinubu and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, pledging to work for the victory of the Rainbow Coalition in the 2027 general elections. Fubara spoke on Tuesday at the unveiling of the coalition’s candidates in Rivers State, where he urged members to put past leadership disputes behind them and work together. The governor described the coalition as family, expressing happiness at being reunited with political allies after a crisis that divided the group. “I’m really happy to be here, not just being here, but standing in the midst of my family,” he said. Fubara acknowledged Wike and other political leaders for their roles in his emergence as governor, expressing gratitude that they had come together again for what he described as the collective good of Rivers State. He pledged to support the coalition’s candidates, saying he would do everything within his power to secure their victory. The governor also thanked Tinubu for standing by him during his most difficult period and reaffirmed his commitment to the political bloc led by Wike. “I’m here with all my heart, my soul, and my body, and I will do everything within my power to ensure that we have victory, not just for Mr President, who has stood for me in my most difficult time, but also to ensure that this power still remains in our own bloc,” Fubara said. He described the unveiling as an honour and expressed optimism about the candidates’ performance in the January 2027 elections. The Rainbow Coalition comprises seven political parties that have aligned to field consensus candidates for the elections in Rivers State. They are the All Progressives Congress (APC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Action Alliance (AA), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), Labour Party (LP), Allied Peoples Movement (APM) and Boot Party. However, candidates from only the APC and PDP emerged as the coalition’s consensus candidates for the 2027 elections. The coalition, led by Wike, who is also the national leader of the PDP, unveiled its candidates at a ceremony in Port Harcourt on Tuesday. Former Minority Leader of the House of Representatives, Kingsley Chinda, emerged as the coalition’s governorship candidate on the APC platform, with the current Majority Leader of the Rivers State House of Assembly, Major Jack, as his running mate. For the three senatorial districts, the APC has two candidates, while the PDP has one. Felix Amaechi Obua is the APC candidate for Rivers West, while Senator Allwell Onyesoh is the party’s candidate for Rivers East. Senator Olaka Nwogu of the PDP is the candidate for Rivers South-East. The coalition’s House of Representatives list has 13 candidates, comprising 10 APC members and three PDP members. item.title: ADC-PCC to N’Assembly: Reject Tinubu’s $21bn loan over lack of transparency
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has urged the National Assembly to reject President Bola Tinubu’s proposed $20 billion and £1 billion foreign borrowing unless the Federal Government provides full details of the facilities and demonstrates their benefits to Nigerians. The council said the fresh borrowing would add to the burden on Nigerians already battling rising living costs and increased taxation, questioning why the government was seeking more loans without accounting for previous borrowings and savings from fuel subsidy removal. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC faulted the administration’s borrowing plans, demanding evidence that the funds would translate into tangible improvements in citizens’ lives. “What exactly is President Tinubu borrowing all this money for? Where are the roads, the electricity, the hospitals, the jobs and the critical infrastructure that should justify this relentless accumulation of debt? Nigerians deserve answers,” Ologbondiyan said. He questioned why the government was returning to international creditors while millions of Nigerians struggled to survive the effects of its economic policies. The council warned that continued borrowing without transparent spending and measurable returns could deepen Nigeria’s debt burden, restrict future governments’ policy options and threaten the country’s economic sovereignty. “This is not a sustainable path to national development. It is a dangerous attempt to mortgage the future of Nigeria and generations yet unborn,” Ologbondiyan said. The ADC-PCC demanded that Tinubu publish a comprehensive account of all domestic and foreign borrowing since May 29, 2023, including a breakdown of revenue realised from subsidy removal and how the funds had been spent. It also called for full disclosure of the proposed loans’ purposes, interest rates, repayment periods, fees, conditions and any collateral or guarantees attached to the facilities. “Nigeria cannot borrow its way out of poor economic management. Borrowing must be tied to clearly defined national priorities, transparent expenditure and measurable outcomes. Anything less is an injustice to the Nigerian people,” the council said. It urged lawmakers to insist on accountability and refuse to approve the facilities until the Federal Government establishes their necessity, sustainability and tangible benefits to Nigerians. item.title: Nasarawa NDC Publicity Secretary quits party, declares support for SDP candidate
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Publicity Secretary of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Nasarawa State, Mr Joseph Danjuma, has resigned from the party and declared support for the Social Democratic Party (SDP) governorship candidate, former Inspector-General of Police, Abubakar Adamu. Danjuma announced his resignation in a letter titled “Letter of Resignation” addressed to the state chairman of the NDC, citing a lack of opportunity to perform his duties as the party’s spokesperson. “I wish to humbly resign my membership and position as the Publicity Secretary of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Nasarawa State Chapter, with immediate effect,” he stated. Explaining his decision, he added: “My decision follows the lack of opportunity to perform my role as the spokesperson of the party in the state.” Following his resignation, Danjuma declared his intention to join Adamu’s campaign ahead of the 2027 governorship election. “With this development, I hereby fully join the campaign train of Ex-IGP Adamu. Thank you,” he said. Danjuma, a journalist who has worked with print and broadcast media organisations, previously served as Chief Press Secretary to former Nasarawa State Deputy Governor, Hon. Dameshi Luka. He had earlier expressed support for Adamu at a rally organised under the auspices of the Alago Support Group. Speaking at the event, Danjuma said the group was formed out of a desire for the Alago people to participate actively in decisions concerning the political future of Nasarawa State. He said the group considered Adamu a suitable candidate based on his record of public service and experience as a former police chief. Danjuma also highlighted Adamu’s connections with the Alago community, noting that he had attended school with some prominent sons and daughters of the area in Obi and had maternal ties to the people. “We have resolved that we will no longer be onlookers or fence-sitters while the political destiny of our dear state is being decided. The time to participate, to take a stand and to take our destiny in our own hands is now,” he said. He maintained that members of the Alago community should be free to support candidates of their choice, citing Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution, which guarantees freedom of peaceful assembly and association. Efforts to obtain a reaction from the NDC chairman in Nasarawa State, Hon. Dogo Shammah, regarding Danjuma’s resignation and his stated reason for leaving the party were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: 2027: Atiku Not A Man You Can Take His Word To The Bank – Wike
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has questioned the credibility of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, accusing him of frequently changing his position on political matters. Wike spoke on Tuesday at the unveiling of candidates of the Rivers State Rainbow Coalition, where he criticised the consistency of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate. Drawing on his past political dealings with Atiku, Wike recalled supporting the former vice-president’s presidential ambition in 2019 and running against him in the Peoples Democratic Party’s (PDP) presidential primary in 2022. “I pray you never know him, [Atiku Abubakar]. I ran with him in the 2022 presidential primaries. In 2019, I was one of the biggest sponsors for that presidential election,” he said. Wike questioned Atiku’s reliability, declaring, “He’s not a man that you can go to the bank with his words.” ﻿ The minister alleged that Atiku frequently changed his position, making it difficult to rely on his statements. “He tells you one thing in the morning, he tells you another thing in the afternoon. He tells you something in the evening, the next morning he tells you a different thing,” Wike said.
